title: Define performance targets budgets and benchmark registry
goal: Create the strict performance registry describing measurable targets, metric semantics, budgets, benchmark environments, change triggers and not-applicable behavior before any regression runner can make claims.
invariants: performance claims require representative measured evidence
no runtime target is fabricated when no product-runtime boundary exists
benchmark noise cannot silently relax an explicit budget
expensive performance work is triggered proportionally rather than on every trivial change
security_properties: benchmark inputs and result files are untrusted data, never executable configuration
performance tooling remains development-only unless separately approved
resource tests use explicit bounded time and memory limits
acceptance_tests: unit tests reject invalid units budgets owners and nonexistent runtime targets

performance_budget.rationale: this layer governs performance measurement overhead as well as product targets
metrics: registry audit target: sub-second on metadata-only repositories

rollback.strategy: revert the E6 unit while retaining verified E0-E5 controls

definition_of_done: metric units and aggregation semantics are closed enums
every registered target has owner path, workload, environment and budget
runtime targets must map to real product-runtime boundaries
no-runtime repositories report not-applicable rather than pass-by-assumption
